items.title: Ray Brown interviewed by Monk Rowe, Scottsdale, AZ, April 16, 2000
items.q: he picked up another guy two weeks later, Milt Jackson... All you want to do is get on the bandstand and play that music. Because if you’ve got enough money to eat — at times Jackson and I only had money just for dinner.

ctx.x: Featured you again, took advantage of your talents with “One Bass Hit” and all those tunes.

Well you know I always say to people, I said first of all for Dizzy Gillespie to assemble a band like that, I mean you know the guy’s got to have a lot of smarts to put a band together like that. And he picked up another guy two weeks later, Milt Jackson. So he knows what’s going on. I mean everybody that he put in that band turned out to be some kind of monster on their instrument. So he had some knowledge. He could listen to somebody and say okay, come here.
What was it like from a business sense and financially to try to keep a group like that together?
